Definition: Percentage of the national population covered by at least one 4G/LTE mobile network signal, whether or not they subscribe to the service. 4G is the practical minimum for meaningful broadband connectivity enabling digital services.
redteam_note: Only one source for a substantive score — corroborate.
revision_notes: GSMA (Nov 2025) states Uganda has 96% 4G population coverage, supporting code 5, but a UCC-backed investment study reported by CEO East Africa (Jun 2026) puts current 4G coverage at only 82%, needing USD280m to reach 95%. These two recent authoritative-ish sources conflict by 14 points. Not confident enough to assert either figure over the other, so leaving the code unchanged pending human review of which measurement basis (signal presence vs quality-assured coverage) is correct.

Definition: Affordability of mobile broadband data, measured as the cost of a basic mobile data plan (1-2GB) as a percentage of GNI per capita. The UN Broadband Commission target is below 2% of monthly GNI per capita. Affordability is the single largest barrier to internet adoption in Africa.
redteam_note: Only one source for a substantive score — corroborate.
revision_notes: The 2018 A4AI figure (~8.76% of GNI per capita) is stale. digitaldevelopment.org's mAccess diagnostic lists Uganda's mobile prepaid 1GB basket at 2.17% of GNI per capita, and ITU's 2025 ICT Price Baskets report shows African mobile baskets have fallen to a 3-7% regional range in 2024, both indicating substantial improvement since 2018. Revised to Moderate (2-5%). Exact year of the digitaldevelopment.org figure is not fully certain, so moderate rather than high confidence.

Definition: Percentage of individuals who used the internet (from any location, via any device) in the last three months. This measures actual internet adoption beyond network availability, capturing the combined effect of infrastructure, affordability, digital literacy, and relevance.
redteam_note: Only one source for a substantive score — corroborate.
revision_notes: Confirmed. World Bank/ITU data show 15.3% for 2023 and DataReportal (Kepios) shows 22-28% for 2024/2025 — both fall within the 15-29% band, supporting the original code. Flagging for awareness: World Bank's own 2024 figure shows an anomalous drop to 8.9% (inconsistent with the 2023 value and DataReportal), and Uganda's Ministry of Finance is separately quoted claiming 64% penetration — both outliers not used to change the score but worth human review given the scale of disagreement across sources.

Definition: Whether the country has an operational Internet Exchange Point (IXP) and its maturity. IXPs enable local internet traffic to be exchanged domestically rather than being routed internationally, reducing latency, costs, and dependence on foreign infrastructure. Critical for local digital ecosystem development.
Value Name: Mature IXP ecosystem with broad participation
redteam_note: Only one source for a substantive score — corroborate.
revision_notes: UIXP's own 2024 annual report states the exchange began and ended 2024 with 32 connected networks and ~40Gbps peak traffic, and explicitly cites local market conditions (high taxes, a lingering Facebook ban, Google's withdrawal from remote peering) as suppressing growth. This is an active, moderately-participated single IXP rather than a mature, broadly-participated ecosystem comparable to larger African exchanges. Revised down to 'Active IXP(s) with moderate participation'.

Definition: Unique mobile subscriber penetration rate as a percentage of the total population. Measures the proportion of individuals who subscribe to a mobile service (not SIM cards, which can be multiple per person). Mobile phones are the primary device for internet access in Africa.
redteam_note: Only one source for a substantive score — corroborate.
revision_notes: The original source (an 'Internet_users' URL, also duplicated for the Internet Usage Rate row) appears mislabelled and reflects SIM/connections penetration (76-83%), not unique subscribers. Uganda's own regulator, UCC, reports in its 2023 Annual Communications Sector Report that Unique Mobile Subscriptions were 13.3 million against Registered Subscriptions of 45 million — i.e. roughly 27-28% of Uganda's ~47.8 million population are unique mobile subscribers once multi-SIM ownership is removed. This is a substantial downward correction from 70%+ to 25-39%, based on the definitionally-correct primary regulator data.

revision_notes: Confirmed with a fresher, more authoritative source: UCC's 2023 Annual Communications Sector Report records 15 million smartphones against 37 million active (90-day) mobile subscriptions, i.e. approximately 41% of connections are smartphones — comfortably within the 40-59% band, replacing the weaker 2021 GeoPoll blog estimate.

Definition: The availability and presence of major cloud service providers (hyperscale and regional) operating in or serving the country with local or near-local infrastructure. Cloud availability determines access to scalable computing resources for government, business, and startups.
Value Name: Served remotely from distant regions only (>100ms latency)
redteam_note: Only one source for a substantive score — corroborate.
revision_notes: The original source discussed a South African Google Cloud region and did not actually address Uganda-specific availability. Liquid Intelligent Technologies launched a Microsoft Azure Stack hub physically in Uganda in 2024, and Raxio Data Centre launched the ABQ Cloud sovereign cloud platform in Uganda in 2026 in partnership with the ICT ministry. Together these represent at least one major provider with local presence, so the code is revised up from 'served remotely only' to 'at least one major provider with local presence or edge node'.

revision_notes: Confirmed. Two independent aggregators of the ITU Global Cybersecurity Index 2024 both place Uganda at ~83 (83.10 and 82.94 respectively), well above the 80 threshold for this variable's top band. Consistent with the ITU's own 2024 GCI methodology and release.

Definition: Whether the country has enacted comprehensive data protection and privacy legislation. A foundational legal requirement for building trust in digital public infrastructure and for enabling secure cross-border data flows under frameworks like the AU Convention on Cyber Security and Personal Data Protection.
Value Name: Legislation enacted with Data Protection Authority established
redteam_note: Only one source for a substantive score — corroborate.
revision_notes: Confirmed directly from primary legal sources: the Data Protection and Privacy Act No. 9 of 2019 establishes the Personal Data Protection Office (PDPO), operational under NITA-U, with supporting Data Protection and Privacy Regulations 2021. Fully supports 'legislation enacted with Data Protection Authority established'.

Definition: The presence and tier quality of commercial/colocation data center facilities operating in the country. Commercial data centers provide the physical infrastructure for hosting cloud services, content delivery, and enterprise applications domestically.
Value Name: At least one Tier III facility
redteam_note: Only one source for a substantive score — corroborate.
revision_notes: Confirmed. Raxio's own UG1 facility (Namanve) is Uganda's only Uptime Institute Tier III-certified, carrier-neutral data centre (400 racks, 1.5MW). Xalam Frontier Markets' 2025 Data Centre Market Brief confirms Raxio remains the sole carrier-neutral facility, with the rest of the market comprising sub-scale MNO/telco server rooms — consistent with 'at least one Tier III facility' rather than multiple.

redteam_note: Only one source for a substantive score — corroborate.

Definition: Frequency and severity of power outages experienced by businesses and households. Based on World Bank Enterprise Surveys, Afrobarometer, or national utility data. Reflects the quality of electricity supply beyond mere access — critical for running ICT equipment and data infrastructure.
redteam_note: Only one source for a substantive score — corroborate.
revision_notes: Flagged for human review rather than recalculated. The original comment cites '84 outages/month', which if accurate would indicate near-daily outages (Severe, code 1), not the 'weekly/poor' code 2 that was actually assigned — an internal inconsistency. A 2023 academic study (Migisha et al., using UETCL/Umeme data) reports thousands of interruption events per month at distribution-system level, but this is an aggregate network-wide figure, not a directly comparable per-customer/per-household outage frequency, so it cannot be cleanly mapped to this variable's scale. ERA publishes annual Electricity Supply Industry Performance Reports that likely contain the correct SAIDI/SAIFI-based figures but the specific per-customer outage frequency could not be confirmed in this pass. Recommend human review using ERA's Electricity Supply Industry Performance Report and World Bank Enterprise Survey firm-level outage data.

Definition: Percentage of total electricity generation from renewable sources (hydro, solar, wind, geothermal, biomass). Indicates energy sustainability and potential for distributed power solutions relevant to ICT infrastructure in off-grid areas.
redteam_note: Only one source for a substantive score — corroborate.
revision_notes: Confirmed with a stronger primary source: the IEA's 2023 Uganda energy review states approximately 92% of generating capacity is renewable (about 80% large hydro, 8% bagasse, 4.5% solar PV), and the accompanying OECD/IEA tables put renewable share of energy consumption at 92.5%, rising toward >95%. Comfortably within the 75%+ band. Note the original comment's claim of '~100% hydro' overstates the hydro-specific share, though the total renewable share does support the code.

Definition: The gap between urban and rural electricity access rates. A smaller gap indicates more equitable energy distribution, critical for ensuring ICT infrastructure can serve the whole population, not just cities.
redteam_note: Only one source for a substantive score — corroborate.
revision_notes: Broadly confirmed, though with some residual uncertainty. World Bank data (via IndexMundi) show urban access at 69.87% and rural at 32.83% (most recent split available, 2020), a gap of ~37pp, consistent with the 21-40pp band. SEforALL Africa Hub separately cites urban ~60%/rural ~18% (gap ~42pp, undated), which would tip into the next band up (41-60pp). Given the closeness to the boundary and unclear vintage of the SEforALL figure, keeping the original band but flagging for human review if a precise, current urban/rural split is needed.

revision_notes: Confirmed with a stronger, primary-data-based source: CEO East Africa, citing the Africa: The Big Deal database, reports Ugandan startups raised $19m in 2024 (up from $4.8m in 2023, ranked 11th in Africa) — well below the $50m+ threshold for 'Established', supporting 'Developing' with regular but modest funding rounds and several active hubs.

redteam_note: Only one source for a substantive score — corroborate.
revision_notes: Correcting a banding error rather than a data error: the Afrobarometer AD515 report (cited in the original comment) states 26% of Ugandan adults own an internet-enabled mobile phone, a reasonable literacy proxy — but 26% falls in the 25-39% band, not the 10-24% band that was actually assigned. redteam_note: Only one source for a substantive score — corroborate.
revision_notes: Tentatively confirmed but flagged for review: GSMA's Mobile Gender Gap Report 2024 explicitly lists Uganda among countries where the gender gap in mobile internet adoption remains 'wide' even though the ownership gap is small, qualitatively supporting a continuing moderate-to-large usage gap. However, UCC's own 2023 report shows a Gender Parity Score of 0.986 for mobile access/ownership (near parity), a different metric to internet use. Could not find a precise, current percentage for Uganda's mobile-internet gender gap specifically, so kept the original band but recommend human review to pin down an exact figure.
